findings.folded_into: the follow-on node that re-runs the certificate-state half; the title is a one-line string change there
findings.summary: The right panel title is 'geometry term to central difference', which omits 'replaced by'. As rendered, a reader sees a headline that reads as a comparison of the geometry term against a central difference, not as the same assembly with that term substituted by its own central difference. The caption disambiguates, but the panel title alone misstates what the panel shows.

findings.folded_into: the follow-on node that re-runs the certificate-state half of bank-jacobian-mismatch with a longer wall (same command, no driver change), after which the same plot draws both states from the colour map that already defines 'certificate'
findings.summary: The figure carries one state only. The section 3 brief asks for relative mismatch per direction class at the stalled and the certificate state, and the rendered PNG shows a single bar per class in each panel, under a one-entry legend reading 'stalled 1e-2'. The certificate state is absent because its measurement was cut short by the allocation wall, and the caption and fragment say so honestly; the consequence is that the reader cannot see the stalled-versus-certificate comparison the figure was commissioned for.

findings.exempted_reason: colour is a one-line change in one constant and does not affect whether the figure can be read; the next node that redraws this figure to add the certificate state picks the feature colour under the rule then
findings.summary: The stalled-state bars are drawn in #c0392b, a saturated red, while every bar in both panels sits below the acceptance floor of 1e-6. The repository's plotting rules reserve red for a limit being broken, so the colour signals a failure the data do not show: the panels' message is that the assembled Jacobian is inside the floor across every class.

findings.folded_into: the same follow-on node that redraws the figure with the certificate state, at which point the legend has two entries and earns its place
findings.summary: The figure-level legend carries a single entry, 'stalled 1e-2', which duplicates what the caption already states and spends the top margin on a distinction with nothing to distinguish. With one series the state could be named in the caption alone, or directly on the panel, freeing the space and removing the implication that a second series was meant to be there.

review.note: Read-only figure review. Judged only from the rendered PNG named in the review brief; the drawing script was read for anchoring only. No file was edited, redrawn or relabelled.

rubric_items.contrast: Text clears its background: near-black tick and axis labels on white, and the dark-red bars read cleanly against white at their full height. No label is greyed or washed out.
rubric_items.data_ink: The data carry the weight: twelve solid bars over six direction classes and two panels, one dotted acceptance-floor line at 1e-6, no gradients, shadows or decorative fills. The only redundancy is a one-entry legend, which the caption already supplies (see finding).
rubric_items.decoration: No gradient, no background fill, no gridlines; top and right spines are removed and the only added rule is the dotted 1e-6 acceptance floor, whose extent is itself data and which the caption names.
rubric_items.label_collision: No label is clipped, overlapping another, or over the bars: panel titles and the figure legend sit in clear space above the axes, the ordinate label clears the tick labels, the two-line 'normal form' tick wraps with clear space beneath it, and the x tick labels are fully visible in both panels.
rubric_items.legibility: Readable at a glance: two panels at 1400x720 px, 14 pt panel titles and tick labels, 16 pt shared ordinate label, log ordinate spanning 1e-10 to just above 1e-6. One exception: the right panel's headline, 'geometry term to central difference', drops the words 'replaced by' and so reads as a comparison of the geometry term against a central difference rather than as the same comparison with that term substituted (see finding).
rubric_items.table_form: The image does not depict a table in picture form: six direction classes compared across two treatments on a log ordinate is a magnitude comparison the eye does better than a column of numbers, and the brief asks for this figure beside the tables rather than instead of them.
